chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ya'qub ibn Yaqteen said:

I asked a virtuous man about a man who prayed on a cloudy day not facing the qibla, then the sun rose while he was still within the prayer time. Should he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the qibla, even if he had exerted himself to determine the qibla? Will his prayer suffice? He said: 'He repeats it if it was within the time; and if the time has passed, there is no repetition for him.'

key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: The direction of prayer towards the Kaaba in Mecca
key_terms.الْوَقْت: The specific time period for a prayer
key_terms.تَحَرَّى: To strive or exert effort to determine
key_terms.يَوْمِ سَحَابٍ: A cloudy day, implying obscured visibility of celestial bodies

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to repeat their prayer if they prayed facing the wrong qibla due to clouds but realized the mistake before the prayer time ended?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ja'far al-Sadiq (via Abd al-Salih) clarifies that if one prays facing an incorrect qibla due to genuine effort (ijtihad) under cloudy skies, the prayer is valid but must be repeated if the correct direction is discovered while the prayer time remains. However, if the time expires before the correction is made, the prayer is considered complete and no repetition is required, reflecting the Shia principle of excusing errors in qibla determination when due to valid circumstances. This ruling underscores the importance of intention and effort in ritual purity and prayer validity within Ja'fari jurisprudence.
